newsitem.title: UK: UK says has not decided Benefits Agency unit sale.
newsitem.headline: UK says has not decided Benefits Agency unit sale.

text.p: A government spokesman on Thursday denied a press report that ministers had decided to proceed with the privatisation of the Benefits Agency medical service which had been planned by the outgoing Conservative administration.
"It is still being reviewed and no decisions have been taken," the spokesman for the Social Security Department said.
However, trade union sources insisted that a Guardian report saying staff representatives were told at a meeting on Wednesday that the sell-off would go ahead was accurate.
Four companies accepted a request by outgoing Social Services Secretary Peter Lilley to bid for the service -- BMI International, Sema Group Plc, Capita Group Plc and Andersen Consulting.
The spokesman confirmed that a meeting was held on Wednesday to discuss the issue, but added: "The thrust of policy has yet to be decided."

When Lilley first revealed the plan last October, Labour's social security spokesman, Henry McLeish, said the decision showed that the Government was putting commercial considerations ahead of all others.
"We have serious concerns about this. It is putting dogma before everything else," he said.
McLeish is now a Scottish Office minister in charge of the government's devolution plans.
